scenarios.title: Rare countermodel closed by a trigger
scenarios.scenario: A selector s normally agrees with an output x; the opposite branch requires every trigger bit to be true.
scenarios.intervention: Add one clause forbidding the all-true trigger.
scenarios.rationale: Model sampling can confuse a highly biased literal with a backbone. Closing the escape makes it genuinely forced.
scenarios.equation: (s OR t_i) for all i, x <-> s; intervention: OR_i NOT t_i.

scenarios.title: Reconvergent implication orientation
scenarios.scenario: A connected equality network carries a hidden anchor through many paths.
scenarios.intervention: Reverse the anchor polarity while keeping the network.
scenarios.rationale: A cached or partially propagated backbone must change sign throughout the component.
scenarios.equation: x_i <-> x_j on a connected graph; (a OR q) AND (a OR NOT q), then a becomes NOT a.

scenarios.title: One parity sign changes consistency
scenarios.scenario: Pairwise XOR relations close a cycle whose XOR sum is zero.
scenarios.intervention: Flip the parity on the closing edge.
scenarios.rationale: Local consistency of individual clauses does not establish global satisfiability.
scenarios.equation: XOR_i (x_i XOR x_(i+1)) = 0; one RHS flip makes it 1.

scenarios.title: Free parity mode becomes a full backbone
scenarios.scenario: A signed equality tree has two complementary solutions.
scenarios.intervention: Pin one variable with a two-clause anchor.
scenarios.rationale: A single semantic intervention forces an entire correlated component.
scenarios.equation: x_i XOR x_parent(i) = b_i; add (x_1 OR q) AND (x_1 OR NOT q).

scenarios.title: Overlapping cardinality contradiction
scenarios.scenario: A resource pool requires exactly k active items.
scenarios.intervention: Add an at-least-(k+1) requirement on the same pool.
scenarios.rationale: Different cardinality constraints look individually feasible but jointly contradict one another.
scenarios.equation: sum x_i = k versus sum x_i = k AND sum x_i >= k+1.

scenarios.title: Blocking a globally unique witness
scenarios.scenario: A signed connected network plus an anchor has exactly one core assignment.
scenarios.intervention: Add one clause falsified by that complete core assignment.
scenarios.rationale: A long added clause can eliminate the last model despite leaving every variable well formed.
scenarios.equation: F has unique core model m; F AND (OR_i NOT m_i) has none.

scenarios.title: Nearly exchangeable choices
scenarios.scenario: Exactly one interchangeable option is chosen.
scenarios.intervention: Forbid one option using a relation to a fresh signal rather than changing the format.
scenarios.rationale: A symmetry assumption from the control becomes invalid; one variable enters the backbone.
scenarios.equation: sum x_i = 1; add (NOT x_j OR z) AND (NOT x_j OR NOT z).

scenarios.title: Signed symmetry loses one orientation
scenarios.scenario: Variables in two classes are equal within a class and opposite across classes.
scenarios.intervention: Add a disjunction containing literals true in only one orientation.
scenarios.rationale: Polarity-aware symmetry and backbone logic must distinguish the two complementary models.
scenarios.equation: x_i XOR x_j = phase_i XOR phase_j; add a clause selecting one phase.

scenarios.title: Conditional symmetry is not global symmetry
scenarios.scenario: Each choice x_i has its own indicator y_i; options initially exchange together.
scenarios.intervention: Add a cross-condition coupling one option to a different indicator.
scenarios.rationale: Exchanging only the option variables or reusing a former global symmetry can delete valid solutions.
scenarios.equation: sum x_i=1, y_i <-> x_i; add NOT x_a OR y_b for a != b.

scenarios.title: A graph becomes non-bipartite
scenarios.scenario: Two-color constraints lie on a connected bipartite graph.
scenarios.intervention: Add an edge within one color class.
scenarios.rationale: One local edge creates a global odd-cycle obstruction.
scenarios.equation: For each edge enforce x_u XOR x_v=1; the extra edge closes an odd cycle.

scenarios.title: Hidden resource bottleneck
scenarios.scenario: A bipartite assignment graph admits a perfect matching.
scenarios.intervention: Restrict two agents to the same single resource.
scenarios.rationale: Per-agent availability is nonempty but the joint resource allocation is impossible.
scenarios.equation: Exactly one edge per agent, at most one per resource; |N({a,b})|=1<2.

scenarios.title: Color symmetry with a local obstruction
scenarios.scenario: A triangle and an extra vertex admit three colors.
scenarios.intervention: Connect the extra vertex to every triangle vertex.
scenarios.rationale: The same color permutations remain available, but the extra clique makes the formula UNSAT.
scenarios.equation: 3-color K3 plus v; intervention completes K4, which needs four colors.

scenarios.title: Circuit output phase intervention
scenarios.scenario: A random acyclic AND/OR/XOR circuit has a planted, fixed input vector and reconvergent paths.
scenarios.intervention: Change the required output from its implied value to its opposite.
scenarios.rationale: Reasoning from local fan-in or an incomplete circuit abstraction can miss the unique output consequence.
scenarios.equation: Inputs fixed by two-clause anchors; Tseitin gate equivalences; assert output b versus NOT b.

scenarios.title: A bridge correlates formerly independent components
scenarios.scenario: Two signed connected components each have two orientations.
scenarios.intervention: Add one parity bridge between the components.
scenarios.rationale: Component decomposition must be updated after the intervention; model count halves without necessarily creating a backbone.
scenarios.equation: F(X) AND G(Y), then AND (x_1 XOR y_1=b).

scenarios.title: Last missing conflict clause
scenarios.scenario: All assignments of a small variable block except one are excluded by full-width clauses.
scenarios.intervention: Insert the single omitted conflict clause.
scenarios.rationale: The last globally surviving witness disappears although there is no empty clause or direct contradictory-unit pair.
scenarios.equation: All 2^k full-width clauses except C_m versus all 2^k clauses.

scenarios.title: Threshold trigger forces a selector
scenarios.scenario: When selector s is false, a pool must have exactly k selected bits; when true the pool is unrestricted.
scenarios.intervention: Raise the guarded lower threshold by one.
scenarios.rationale: Only the trigger branch becomes impossible, creating a selector backbone without making the whole instance UNSAT.
scenarios.equation: (s OR CNF(sum x_i<=k)) AND (s OR CNF(sum x_i>=k)); raise lower bound to k+1.

scenarios.title: Suboptimal one-flip basin with a strict core
scenarios.scenario: Coupled Boolean choices have a cheap all-true basin and an expensive all-false basin.
scenarios.intervention: Increase equality-coupling weight above the total unary preference weight.
scenarios.rationale: A one-flip improving search can remain at a proven suboptimal feasible assignment; the objective is ordinary integer MaxSAT.
scenarios.equation: Soft J*[x_i=x_j], positive units total P, negative anchor B<P. All-true costs B; all-false costs P; J>P+B blocks every core-variable flip.

scenarios.title: Disconnected feasible orientations
scenarios.scenario: A connected hard equality component has two feasible assignments with unequal costs.
scenarios.intervention: Turn soft coupling constraints into hard equalities.
scenarios.rationale: Changing basin requires temporary hard-constraint violations; a feasible incumbent can be suboptimal.
scenarios.equation: Hard x_i=x_j; soft positive units total P and negative anchor B<P.

scenarios.title: Clause majority disagrees with weight majority
scenarios.scenario: Many linked positive proxy preferences compete with one negative preference.
scenarios.intervention: Move the negative weight from just below to just above their total.
scenarios.rationale: Choosing the most numerous satisfied clauses gives the wrong weighted optimum after the intervention.
scenarios.equation: Hard y_i=x; soft (y_i,1), (NOT x,q); optimum min(m,q), winning orientation reverses at q=m.

scenarios.title: Coordinated star-cover exchange
scenarios.scenario: A star graph can be covered by its center or all leaves, with variable selection costs.
scenarios.intervention: Move center cost across the total leaf cost.
scenarios.rationale: Greedy single-vertex deletion cannot exchange the two covers while staying feasible.
scenarios.equation: Hard (c OR l_i); soft NOT c cost W, NOT l_i cost w_i; optimum min(W,sum_i w_i).

scenarios.title: Frustrated weighted cycle
scenarios.scenario: Weighted parity preferences form a consistent cycle.
scenarios.intervention: Flip the closing parity relation.
scenarios.rationale: The inconsistent cycle must pay at least one edge weight; sacrificing the wrong edge is a measurable cost gap.
scenarios.equation: Soft XOR edge relations, same weight for their two CNF clauses; odd parity inconsistency costs the minimum edge weight.

scenarios.title: Shared exclusion cores
scenarios.scenario: Positive vertex preferences compete under pairwise exclusion constraints.
scenarios.intervention: Add overlapping exclusions around a high-degree vertex.
scenarios.rationale: Counting overlapping conflicts independently can overestimate a lower bound or choose poor relaxations.
scenarios.equation: Hard NOT x_u OR NOT x_v; soft (x_v,w_v): optimum = total weights minus maximum-weight independent set.

scenarios.title: Shared repair covers many demands
scenarios.scenario: Each demand is a disjunction of possible repairs, each with an activation cost.
scenarios.intervention: Add one shared repair to several demands.
scenarios.rationale: Repairing each demand independently misses savings from one shared activation.
scenarios.equation: Hard OR_{v in S_j} x_v; soft (NOT x_v,w_v): minimum-weight hitting set.

scenarios.title: Capacity threshold and close weights
scenarios.scenario: At most k rewards can be selected.
scenarios.intervention: Raise a formerly excluded item's weight above a selected item's weight.
scenarios.rationale: A stale ranking or an overaggressive weight bucket keeps a feasible but suboptimal solution.
scenarios.equation: Hard sum x_i<=k; soft (x_i,w_i); optimum is sum of the n-k smallest weights.

scenarios.title: No feasible single-bit move
scenarios.scenario: Exactly k choices must remain active, with weighted rewards.
scenarios.intervention: Add weak pairwise agreement preferences to change the best exchange.
scenarios.rationale: Every one-bit change violates feasibility; improvement requires a coordinated two-bit exchange or temporary infeasibility.
scenarios.equation: Hard sum x_i=k; soft unary rewards plus equality preferences on selected random pairs.

scenarios.title: Small residual after competing preferences
scenarios.scenario: Opposite soft preferences on a hard-linked component mostly cancel.
scenarios.intervention: Change one weight by a small amount across the residual balance point.
scenarios.rationale: Dropping a residual or forgetting a constant cost can reverse the optimum or misreport its value.
scenarios.equation: Hard y_i=x; soft (x,a),(NOT x,b),(y_i,c_i); compare b with a+sum c_i.

scenarios.title: One high priority trades against many lower priorities
scenarios.scenario: Exactly one of two assignment bundles is feasible.
scenarios.intervention: Change the high-level preference across the total lower-level loss.
scenarios.rationale: Treating finite weights as absolute priorities changes the actual weighted problem.
scenarios.equation: Hard bundle equivalences/oppositions; soft lower rewards sum L versus a high preference of weight L-1 or L+1.

scenarios.title: Coupling breaks objective additivity
scenarios.scenario: Two independently optimized bundles prefer opposite orientations.
scenarios.intervention: Add one hard equality across the bundles.
scenarios.rationale: The sum of old component optima is no longer achievable after coupling.
scenarios.equation: min f(X)+min g(Y) becomes min_{x_1=y_1}(f(X)+g(Y)).

scenarios.title: A complete weighted conflict cover
scenarios.scenario: Full-width soft clauses exclude every core assignment except one.
scenarios.intervention: Insert the omitted soft clause with a positive weight.
scenarios.rationale: The optimum changes from zero to the least clause weight, so a stale zero-cost model is invalid.
scenarios.equation: Each full-width clause is false at exactly one assignment; after all 2^k are present OPT=min_C w_C.

scenarios.title: Competing signed pair interactions
scenarios.scenario: A connected graph mixes weighted equality, inequality, and unary preferences.
scenarios.intervention: Flip the preferred relation on one influential edge.
scenarios.rationale: A local sign change can rearrange the global optimum; local edge satisfaction alone is insufficient.
scenarios.equation: Minimize sum_e w_e*[x_u XOR x_v != b_e] plus unary penalties.

scenarios.title: A conjunction trigger disables the cheap branch
scenarios.scenario: A selector controls two feasible cost basins and is linked to a multi-bit trigger.
scenarios.intervention: Require all trigger bits, thereby forcing the more expensive selector orientation.
scenarios.rationale: A semantic trigger changes the feasible optimum rather than the input syntax; cached incumbents must be rechecked.
scenarios.equation: t_1 AND ... AND t_k -> s; s=false costs B, s=true costs P>B; add hard t_i=true.

scenarios.title: Very attractive infeasible assignment
scenarios.scenario: A hard capacity constraint rules out selecting every profitable item.
scenarios.intervention: Add a hard exclusion between two high-reward items.
scenarios.rationale: Soft improvement must never be reported as a feasible solution if it violates even one hard constraint.
scenarios.equation: Hard sum x_i<=k plus NOT x_a OR NOT x_b; soft (x_i,w_i). All weights remain small and positive.
